references.text: The priests shall not make bald patches on their heads, nor shave the edges of their beards, nor cut marks in their flesh. This extends the prohibition against cutting the body to apply specifically to the priests.
The Israelites, who are the Lord's people, shall not cut themselves or shave their foreheads for the dead. This repeats the prohibition against cutting oneself in connection with mourning rituals.
The prophets of Baal cut themselves with swords and spears until blood flowed, as part of their pagan worship. This illustrates the pagan practice that Leviticus 19:28 forbids.
Jeremiah prophesies that no one shall cut themselves for the dead in the land. This refers back to the original prohibition in the Mosaic Law.
Men came with shaved beards, torn clothes, and marks of cutting on their bodies. This shows that the practice of cutting oneself continued despite the prohibition.
Gaza has become bald; Ashkelon is silent. How long will you cut yourself? This uses the image of cutting as an expression of grief.
The body is a temple for the Holy Spirit, and believers do not belong to themselves but have been bought with a price. This provides a New Testament basis for treating the body with respect.
